title: Adipocytes-induced ANGPTL4/KLF4 axis drives glycolysis and metastasis in triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: Yin, Dou; Fang, Nana; Zhu, Yaling; Bao, Xiaoqing; Yang, Juan; Zhang, Qingyu; Wang, Ruimeng; Huang, Jiahui; Wu, Qibing; Ma, Fang; Wei, Xiaohui
journal: Journal of experimental & clinical cancer research : CR
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脂肪细胞通过ANGPTL4/KLF4轴驱动三阴性乳腺癌糖酵解与转移，虽涉及KLF4转录因子与ANGPTL4的蛋白-蛋白对接，但核心是肿瘤代谢与临床关联，非TF-DNA结合互作建模，且方法以实验为主，仅少量对接，与本课题匹配度低。
abstract: BACKGROUND: The adipocyte-rich tumor microenvironment (TME) is recognized as a key factor in promoting cancer progression. A distinct characteristic of peritumoral adipocytes is their reduced lipid content and the acquisition of a proinflammatory phenotype. However, the underlying mechanisms by which adipocytes rewire metabolism and boost tumor progression in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain poorly understood. METHODS: We utilized transcriptomic analysis, bioinformatic analysis, metabolic flux analysis, protein-protein docking, gene and protein expression profiling, in vivo metastasis analysis and breast cancer specimens to explore how adipocytes reprogram tumor metabolism and progression in TNBC. RESULTS: Our findings reveal that Angiopoietin-like 4 (ANGPTL4) exhibits significantly higher expression levels in adipocyte-rich tumor circumstance compared to the symbiotic environment lacking of adipocyte. Furthermore, ANGPTL4 expression in tumor cells is essential for adipocyte-driven glycolysis and metastasis. Interleukin 6 (IL-6), enriched in cancer-associated adipocytes, and lipolysis-derived free fatty acids (FFAs) released from adipocytes, amplify ANGPTL4-mediated glycolysis and metastasis through activation of STAT3 and PPARalpha pathways in TNBC cells. Additionally, ANGPTL4 interacts with transcription factor KLF4 and enhances KLF4 activity, which further drives glycolysis and metastasis, whereas KLF4 knockdown attenuates migration and glycolysis in TNBC cells. Importantly, Elevated ANGPTL4 and KLF4 expression was observed in metastatic breast cancer specimens compared to non-metastatic cases and was positively correlated with poor prognosis. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our results uncover a complex metabolic interaction between adipocytes and TNBC cells that promotes tumor aggressiveness. ANGPTL4 emerges as a key mediator in this process, making it a promising therapeutic target to inhibit TNBC progression.
abstract_zh: 背景：富含脂肪细胞的肿瘤微环境（TME）被认为是促进癌症进展的关键因素。肿瘤周围脂肪细胞的一个显著特征是脂质含量减少并获得促炎表型。然而，脂肪细胞在 triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) 中重新编程代谢并促进肿瘤进展的潜在机制仍知之甚少。方法：我们利用转录组分析、生物信息学分析、代谢通量分析、蛋白质-蛋白质对接、基因和蛋白质表达谱分析、体内转移分析以及乳腺癌标本，探讨脂肪细胞如何重编程 TNBC 中的肿瘤代谢和进展。结果：我们的发现揭示，与缺乏脂肪细胞的共生环境相比，富含脂肪细胞的肿瘤环境中 Angiopoietin-like 4 (ANGPTL4) 的表达水平显著更高。此外，肿瘤细胞中 ANGPTL4 的表达对脂肪细胞驱动的糖酵解和转移至关重要。癌症相关脂肪细胞中富集的 Interleukin 6 (IL-6) 以及脂肪细胞释放的脂解衍生游离脂肪酸 (FFAs)，通过激活 TNBC 细胞中的 STAT3 和 PPARalpha 通路，放大 ANGPTL4 介导的糖酵解和转移。此外，ANGPTL4 与转录因子 KLF4 相互作用并增强 KLF4 活性，这进一步驱动糖酵解和转移，而 KLF4 敲低则减弱 TNBC 细胞中的迁移和糖酵解。重要的是，与未转移病例相比，转移性乳腺癌标本中观察到 ANGPTL4 和 KLF4 表达升高，并与不良预后正相关。结论：总体而言，我们的结果揭示了脂肪细胞和 TNBC 细胞之间促进肿瘤侵袭性的复杂代谢相互作用。ANGPTL4 在此过程中作为关键介质出现，使其成为抑制 TNBC 进展的有前景的治疗靶点。
